title: Learn RL from zero
tagline: How machines learn by trying things, explained for anyone who has done JEE Mains maths. No machine learning needed. By the end you can train a bot of your own.

parts.title: Foundations
parts.blurb: What reinforcement learning is, the little maths it leans on, and just enough Python.

chapters.title: Welcome to RL
chapters.summary: Watch a clumsy agent learn a game by trial and error, and meet the loop that every RL problem shares.

chapters.title: The maths toolkit
chapters.summary: Sums, averages, expected value, slopes and a few friends. The only maths we need, rebuilt from the ground up.

chapters.title: Python and NumPy, just enough
chapters.summary: Arrays, random numbers with seeds, and your first tiny experiment.

parts.title: Choices and consequences
parts.blurb: From one decision to a whole sequence of them, and how to plan when you know the rules.

chapters.title: Bandits: try the unknown or stick with what works?
chapters.summary: Five slot machines and a hundred coins. Your first learning agent, and the exploration versus exploitation trade-off.

chapters.title: Markov decision processes
chapters.summary: States, actions, rewards and why the future is worth a little less than now.

chapters.title: Value functions and the Bellman equation
chapters.summary: How good is it to be here? Answered with a small system of equations you can solve by hand.

chapters.title: Dynamic programming: planning when you know the rules
chapters.summary: Policy evaluation, policy iteration and value iteration, with a grid world you can poke at.

parts.title: Learning from experience
parts.blurb: What to do when you do not know the rules and can only learn by playing.

chapters.title: Monte Carlo: learn from whole games
chapters.summary: Play a lot, average what happened, get better.

chapters.title: Temporal-difference learning and Q-learning
chapters.summary: Do not wait until the end to learn. The idea behind most of modern RL.

chapters.title: When tables get too big
chapters.summary: Why we need to guess about states we have never seen, and gradient descent built up from a single variable.

parts.title: Deep reinforcement learning
parts.blurb: Replace the table with a neural network, and learn what to do directly.

chapters.title: Neural networks from scratch
chapters.summary: A neuron is a weighted sum. Stack them, measure the error, and let the chain rule do the learning.

chapters.title: Deep Q-networks
chapters.summary: A network in place of the Q-table, and the two tricks that stop it from falling apart.

chapters.title: Policy gradients
chapters.summary: Do not learn values at all. Learn what to do, and nudge it toward what worked.

parts.title: Many agents
parts.blurb: What changes when the other players are learning too, and how to put it all to work.

chapters.title: Multi-agent RL and self-play
chapters.summary: A moving target, learning by playing yourself, and how rating systems like Elo work.

chapters.title: Bridge: build a Papersseum bot
chapters.summary: The game as an RL problem, a training recipe, and how to pack your policy into one file and submit it.

reference.summary: Every term in the course, in one sentence.

reference.summary: Every symbol and formula on one page.
